I am a proud supporter of a number of Early Access titles, many of which have paid off well for me (Sunless Sea, NeoScavenger, Steam Marines, Don't Starve, and a bunch of others), though I will admit there have been a couple disappointments (Towns, Kinetic Void, Spacebase D9). In my opinion if you buy into Early Access you need to approach the situation differently than if you were purchasing a finished game and really need to manage your expectations. You should also do research to make certain (as much as possible) that your purchase will pay off. You need to view yourself as something in between an investor and a philanthropist or the experience will probably leave a bad taste in your most, especially if the game you buy into fails, sucks, dies in development or just takes 3 fucking years (hi, Prison Architect!).

That said, I can recommend some games that many gamers would have fun with in their current state.

Darkest Dungeon This is currently the only EA game I am playing semiregularly. It is an excellent, somewhat unique, dungeon exploration and party management game. The art design and voice over is excellent, the gameplay itself is relatively simple (characters experience HP and Stress damage during exploration, have special moves based on class and location in the party lineup, higher level abilities and equipment require unlocks that in turn require items from dungeons) but addictive, and the game is approximately 60% complete. You can play for a long time with the current content and it's a good time. The game was recently patched with two new classes (bringing the total to, I dunno, a dozen maybe) and nine new bosses. The final version is still a ways off but in its current state it is playable and enjoyable, just not completable. Development is active.

Prison Architect I joked before about how long this game has taken in development but the current version is very nearly complete and the plan is to release the Final by the end of the year. Updates come monthly and are usually fairly substantial. The game itself tasks you with building, maintaining, and expanding a modern prison and it is impressively complicated. It is not disimilar from a very specialized version of Dwarf Fortress: all the prisoners, guards, whatever have their behavior dictated by AI that is influenced by their environment and the character's personal traits. There is a streak of dark humor running through the game but the subject matter is handled with remarkable responsibility (imo). Also, every month there is a new video explaining whats going on from the lead dev and producer and you can just tell that they are cool dudes. I've been following the company since Darwinia about a decade ago, they're alright.

Underrail I'mnot one hundred percent on this one because it was barely started when I saw their techdemo and gave them money but it's basically an attempt at making a new isometric Fallout-style postapocolypse game. It's still getting monthly updates and has progressed pretty far so it's worth a look, though I can't give it the same seal of approval as the other games I'm listing.

Starbound Starbound is, in simplest terms, scifi Terraria. It has similar gameplay, aesthetics, progression, etc. but everything is bigger and more varied. It also has one of the most toxic communities I've ever encountered on the internet (which is impressive considering I play Elite and Diablo 3, but I have always avoided MOBAs so I guess I'm lucky). The structure Terraria had is lacking (the boss progression, etc), and the game is still in very active development so things change and are added on a weekly basis (well, there's weekly updates at least). Some complain that Terraria is better but Terraria is also several years older and received several massive post release updates. Regardless, there is plenty of content to justify a purchase if you're into this kind of game.

Grim Dawn An ARPG in line with Path of Exile or Diablo 3, Grim Dawn is not quite finished but offers plenty of gameplay for the price. It is not finished, however, and I don't think you can beat the game yet.
